issue.title: Fix cluster alert for watcher/monitoring IndexOutOfBoundsException

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body: If there is an un-resolved cluster alert, but there is no .monitoring-es data for this cluster in the last 2 minutes a run time error in the Watcher transform can occur [1]. This could be due some slow down in getting the .monitoring-es data from source cluster to monitoring cluster. Prior to this commit, the Watch condition can pass if there are un-resolved alerts, but the cluster state could not be found. Since the transform assumes there is a cluster state (green,yellow,red) and could throw an error while trying to read it. This commit prevents passing the condition if the cluster state was not found. Fixes #43184 [1] ``` org.elasticsearch.script.ScriptException: runtime error at org.elasticsearch.painless.PainlessScript.convertToScriptException(PainlessScript.java:94) ~[?:?] at org.elasticsearch.painless.PainlessScript$Script.execute(ctx.vars.email_recipient = (ctx.payload.kibana_settings.hits.total > 0 && ctx.payload.kibana_settings.hits.hits[0]._source.kibana_settings.xpack != null) ? ctx.payload.kibana_settings.hits.hits[0]._source.kibana_settings.xpack.default_admin_email : null;ct ...:1152) ~[?:?] at org.elasticsearch.xpack.watcher.transform.script.ExecutableScriptTransform.doExecute(ExecutableScriptTransform.java:49) ~[x-pack-watcher-7.1.1.jar:7.1.1] ... Caused by: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 0, Size: 0 ``` from .watcher-history: ``` "type" : "script_exception", "reason" : "runtime error", "script_stack" : [ "java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:657)", "java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:433)", "state = ctx.payload.check.hits.hits[0]._source.cluster_state.status;", " ^---- HERE" ], ``` --------- Screen shot of the formatted diff: EDIT: changed the implementation to prevent passing the condition.

issue.title: Fix cluster alert for watcher/monitoring IndexOutOfBoundsExcep…

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body: If a cluster sending monitoring data is unhealthy and triggers an alert, then stops sending data the following exception [1] can occur. This exception stops the current Watch and the behavior is actually correct in part due to the exception. [Simply fixing the exception introduces some incorrect behavior](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/45294). Once the the Watch does not error in the this case, it will result in an incorrectly "resolved" alert due to the way alert resolution is coded. The fix here is two parts a) fix the exception - easy as checking the size of the array before accessing it b) fix the incorrect behavior that results from fixing the exception. - Note - the UI depends on the success/met state for each condition to determine an "OK" or "FIRING" In this scenario, where an unhealthy cluster triggers an alert and then goes silent, it should keep "FIRING" until it hears back that the cluster is green. To keep the Watch "FIRING" either the index action or the email action needs to fire. Since the Watch is neither a "new" alert or a "resolved" alert, we do not want to keep sending an email (that would be non-passive too). Without completely changing the logic of how an alert is resolved allowing the index action to take place would result in the alert being resolved. Since we can not keep "FIRING" either the email or index action (since we don't want to resolve the alert or re-write the logic for alert resolution), we will introduce a 3rd action. A logging action that WILL fire when the cluster is unhealthy. Specifically will fire when there is an unresolved alert and it can not find the cluster state. This logging action is logged at debug, so it should not be noticed much. This logging action serves as an 'anchor' for the UI to keep the state in an a "FIRING" status until the alert is resolved. This commit also increases the versions of the watches. This presents a possible scenario where a cluster starts firing, then goes completely silent forever, the Watch will be "FIRING" forever. This is an edge case that already exists in some scenarios and requires manual intervention to remove that Watch. Fixes #43184 [1] ``` org.elasticsearch.script.ScriptException: runtime error at org.elasticsearch.painless.PainlessScript.convertToScriptException(PainlessScript.java:94) ~[?:?] at org.elasticsearch.painless.PainlessScript$Script.execute(ctx.vars.email_recipient = (ctx.payload.kibana_settings.hits.total > 0 && ctx.payload.kibana_settings.hits.hits[0]._source.kibana_settings.xpack != null) ? ctx.payload.kibana_settings.hits.hits[0]._source.kibana_settings.xpack.default_admin_email : null;ct ...:1152) ~[?:?] at org.elasticsearch.xpack.watcher.transform.script.ExecutableScriptTransform.doExecute(ExecutableScriptTransform.java:49) ~[x-pack-watcher-7.1.1.jar:7.1.1] ... Caused by: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 0, Size: 0 ``` from .watcher-history: ``` "type" : "script_exception", "reason" : "runtime error", "script_stack" : [ "java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:657)", "java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:433)", "state = ctx.payload.check.hits.hits[0]._source.cluster_state.status;", " ^---- HERE" ], ``` ---- To test, enable monitoring and a Kibana email, push the cluster to a unhealthy state: Kibana ``` xpack.monitoring.cluster_alerts.email_notifications.enabled: true xpack.monitoring.cluster_alerts.email_notifications.email_address: alert@example.com ``` ES ``` xpack.monitoring.enabled: true xpack.monitoring.collection.enabled: true ``` Make unhealthy ``` PUT deleteme { "settings": { "number_of_replicas": 100 } } ``` Stop sending metrics ``` PUT _cluster/settings { "transient": { "xpack.monitoring.collection.interval" : "20000s" } } ``` Delete the monitoring index(s) ``` DELETE .monitoring-es-7* ``` Observe that UI stays in a firing state [screen shot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/976291/62655668-198cd080-b928-11e9-9b5b-f9f6902a85d1.png) Fix the cluster ``` DELETE deleteme ``` Allowing monitoring data to flow: ``` PUT _cluster/settings { "transient": { "xpack.monitoring.collection.interval" : null } } ``` A resolved email should now be sent and the UI is now OK Transitional phase that sent the resolved [screen shot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/976291/62655673-1e518480-b928-11e9-8712-1ea260a0e731.png) Stabilized in OK [screen shot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/976291/62655682-214c7500-b928-11e9-96b8-e909135f9ca4.png) --------- A more readable diff:

issue.title: Monitoring: Transform script in elasticsearch_cluster_status.json results in ArrayOutOfBoundsException

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
With monitoring enabled, when a cluster becomes yellow/red there is the possibility of the transform script in the monitoring watch elasticsearch_cluster_status.json resulting in an ArrayOutOfBoundsException.  Two indices are searched against .monitoring-es-* and .monitoring-alerts-6 for information required to use watcher to send an appropriate email related to changes in cluster status.  The condition script ensures that the searches contain results prior to being accessed, but the transform script does not.  Guards should be added to ensure the exception does not occur in the transform script.  However, this is not necessarily simple because without information from the es index it's not possible to know whether the cluster is red/yellow.

This is being seen in production for a number of customers.  But it should be noted that if a cluster is yellow/red this is only a symptom and not the actual problem the cluster may be experiencing.

issue.body:
If a cluster sending monitoring data is unhealthy and triggers an
alert, then stops sending data the following exception [1] can occur.

This exception stops the current Watch and the behavior is actually
correct in part due to the exception. Simply fixing the exception
introduces some incorrect behavior. Now that the Watch does not
error in the this case, it will result in an incorrectly "resolved"
alert.  The fix here is two parts a) fix the exception b) fix the
following incorrect behavior.

a) fixing the exception is as easy as checking the size of the
array before accessing it.

b) fixing the following incorrect behavior is a bit more intrusive

- Note - the UI depends on the success/met state for each condition
to determine an "OK" or "FIRING"

In this scenario, where an unhealthy cluster triggers an alert and
then goes silent, it should keep "FIRING" until it hears back that
the cluster is green. To keep the Watch "FIRING" either the index
action or the email action needs to fire. Since the Watch is neither
a "new" alert or a "resolved" alert, we do not want to keep sending
an email (that would be non-passive too). Without completely changing
the logic of how an alert is resolved allowing the index action to
take place would result in the alert being resolved. Since we can
not keep "FIRING" either the email or index action (since we don't
want to resolve the alert nor re-write the logic for alert resolution),
we will introduce a 3rd action. A logging action that WILL fire when
the cluster is unhealthy. Specifically will fire when there is an
unresolved alert and it can not find the cluster state.
This logging action is logged at debug, so it should be noticed much.
This logging action serves as an 'anchor' for the UI to keep the state
in an a "FIRING" status until the alert is resolved.

This presents a possible scenario where a cluster starts firing,
then goes completely silent forever, the Watch will be "FIRING"
forever. This is an edge case that already exists in some scenarios
and requires manual intervention to remove that Watch.

This changes changes to use a template-like method to populate the 
version_created for the default monitoring watches. The version is 
set to 7.5 since that is where this is first introduced.

Fixes #43184

issue.title: Check hits.total before accessing array in Monitoring Watches

repository.name: kibana
repository.description: Your window into all of your data

issue.body:
Relates to https://github.com/elastic/sdh-kibana/issues/88

I noticed that some of the watches do not have a `(*.hits.total > 0)` safeguard which can cause the following error: 
`Caused by: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 0 out of bounds for length 0`
When trying to access the element like this: `*.hits.hits[0]`.

I would also recommend changing all `*.hits.total != 0` to `*.hits.total > 0`. It’s more consistent and safer against other “falsey” types/values
